title: Minimize the Maximum Adjacent Element Difference
summary: Given an array of integers where some values are -1, you must choose a pair of positive integers (x, y) and replace each -1 with either x or y.
statement: Given an array of integers where some values are -1, you must choose a pair of positive integers (x, y) and replace each -1 with either x or y. The objective is to minimize the maximum absolute difference between adjacent elements after the replacements. Return the smallest possible difference.
constraints: nums has 2–100,000 entries, each -1 or a positive integer up to one billion.
Choose two positive integers once and replace every -1 independently with either chosen value.
Minimize the maximum absolute difference between adjacent values.
hints: For a proposed limit, each known boundary creates an interval of replacement values that can touch it.
Reduce feasibility to stabbing interval families with at most two global values, separating close-value transitions from same-value gap coverage.
Check fixed edges; build boundary and gap-intersection intervals; greedily test two stabbing points, then binary-search the limit.
Two close chosen values can bridge long gaps, while a single-cell gap needs one value in both endpoint intervals; otherwise every gap must use one common covering value.
editorial: Two close chosen values can bridge long gaps, while a single-cell gap needs one value in both endpoint intervals; otherwise every gap must use one common covering value.
